evidence.quote: the Committee concluded that the economic data do not yet provide sufficient confirmation of its baseline outlook to warrant such a reduction.
Thus, the first increases in short-term rates might not occur until the unemployment rate is considerably below 6½ percent.
Apart from some fluctuations due primarily to changes in oil prices, inflation has continued to run below the Committee’s 2 percent longer-term objective.
However, the tightening of financial conditions observed in recent months, if sustained, could slow the pace of improvement in the economy and the labor market.
Notably, at 7.3 percent, the unemployment rate remains well above acceptable levels.
So to the extent that our policy makes conditions—our policy decision today makes conditions just a little bit easier, that's desirable.

parsed.rationale: The Chair explains the surprise decision not to taper, citing insufficient confirmation of the outlook, tighter financial conditions and fiscal risks, while stressing patient rate guidance and below-target inflation. Tapering later this year remains possible, so the signal is dovish but not explicit easing.
